Subject: Unscheduled hotfix: prefetch-induced CPU spikes — immediate mitigation & patch window

Hi Alex / Acme team,

Quick note from on-call: we observed an emerging regression in the runtime prefetch path that can cause sustained CPU spikes and elevated tail latencies for batched requests on certain model families (notably transformer models with long prefix sequences). The issue appears triggered by a combination of a scheduling change in 2029-07-17 and a specific request distribution that increases KV cache churn.

Impact (what we see):
- ~0.5% of hosted inference requests hitting higher 95/99th latency and occasional 503s during heavy batching windows.
- Dedicated pools with older runtime images may experience worker OOMs under sustained load.

Immediate mitigation (what we're doing):
- For hosted customers: Redwood will push an automated hotfix to routing + runtime nodes in the next 30–45 minutes. No action required on your side.
- For Dedicated/private installs: we've published a temporary env knob to disable prefetch: REDWOOD_PREFETCH_DISABLE=true. Setting this will reduce CPU spikes while we roll the patch. See attached customer_mitigation_checklist.txt for exact commands.

Planned window: rolling hotfix starting 11:35 PDT, expected customer-facing corrective behavior within 20–40 minutes of rollout. We'll throttle the roll to maintain SLOs and monitor continuously.

Attachments: prefetch_hotfix_1.0.2.patch (ops artifact), customer_mitigation_checklist.txt, diagnostic-trace-20290719.log (sample traces we observed)

Ask for you:
- Alex: please apply the mitigation knob on any Dedicated hosts if you manage your runtime, otherwise we will cover Hosted.
- Support: mark critical ticket RED-98123 and post updates to the Acme ticket thread.
- Engineering: see the internal CCs — we need a validated rollout and telemetry checks on batched-inference tails.

I'll post status updates here in-thread. Sorry for the short notice — curbing the tail is priority for us.

Thanks,
Ben

Alex — good questions. Short answers:

1) If you don't set REDWOOD_PREFETCH_DISABLE on Dedicated, you may continue to see sporadic elevated latencies and, under extreme sustained pre-prod load, worker OOMs. It will not silently drop traffic; it's a performance degradation risk rather than a correctness failure. If your infra can toggle it during a maintenance window, that would be the safest immediate mitigation.

2) The patch we are deploying updates a scheduling heuristic and fixes a prefetch race. You may see a small, temporary cache-warmup latency bump for a few minutes after a node is restarted or replaced — typical warmup behavior. We will stagger the roll and pre-warm where possible to minimize that impact.

Actionable next steps (for Acme Dedicated pool):
- Run: sudo systemctl set-environment REDWOOD_PREFETCH_DISABLE=true && sudo systemctl restart redwood-runtime
- Verify: watch tail -n 200 /var/log/redwood/diagnostic-trace-*.log for reduced "prefetch: churn" entries and lower CPU in top/htop.

For Hosted: no action required. We'll push and validate the rollout.

We will update this thread at 11:50 with rollout start and 12:10 with initial telemetry.

Ben

Ben / team,

We implemented the hotfix (prefetch_hotfix_1.0.2.patch) and validated on canary. Summary:
- Fixed a race in the prefetch scheduler where evict counters could be decremented twice when a batched request canceled during requeue.
- Added guard to skip prefetch if the scheduling flag prefetch_enabled_v2 is not set.
- Healthcheck added: emits prefetch_churn metric when churn above threshold.

Canary result (11:40–14:30 PDT):
- 99th latency reduced to baseline; no OOMs observed on canary nodes under synthetic replay.
- No customer-facing errors introduced.

We started the rolling push to 20% of Hosted nodes at 15:00 PDT and will continue in waves. Marissa is coordinating the rollout.

Marissa: please post progress updates and whether any Dedicated customers report issues after toggling REDWOOD_PREFETCH_DISABLE.

Stephanie
